answers.explanation: A wider pipe carries more per second, but water doesn't arrive any sooner.
Light in fiber covers about 200,000 km/s. California to the Netherlands and back is about 150 ms, period.
Waiting in router and server queues is what grows when load approaches capacity.
1 RTT for the TCP handshake, 1 for TLS 1.3, and 1 for the request and first byte.
Reusing a connection skips both handshakes. CDNs and batching also fight round trips.
throughput <= window / RTT = 65,536 bytes / 0.1 s, about 655 KB/s, or about 5 Mbit/s.
To keep a link full, the window must be at least the bandwidth-delay product.
